You got that dog in ya.

Buffy's Gym is a small-class strength gym on College St. Every class is coached, nobody trains alone, and yes — the gym is named after the dog.

Not a big box.
A living room with barbells.

There's no open gym floor here. You book a spot in a small class, a coach runs it, and if your shoulder's been acting up, they already know.

Come twice and people greet you by name. Stick around a month and you're in the group photo.

  • Small classes

    Eight people max, one coach, every rep watched.

  • Zero ego

    First-timers and lifers in the same class, lifting side by side.

  • One dog

    Buffy. Her name's on the door.

"I've gotten noticeably prettier since going to this gym." — anonymous, via the notice board

Everybody gets a book.

Paper, not an app. You write down every set you lift; your coach writes back in the margins. Fill one and you start a new one — copying forward only the numbers you haven't beaten yet.

(these are mine — members' own books go here, with permission)

Meet Buffy.

She takes the job seriously: greets everyone at the door, supervises warm-ups from her bed, and hasn't missed a class yet.

"woof." — Buffy

The humans.

Chris and Vanessa own the place — in business and in life — and both coach. Ellen and Miriam round out the crew. Everyone answers to Buffy.

It's not just lifting.

Workshops, pop-ups, karaoke nights, a birthday party for the dog. Everything gets announced on Instagram first — that's the real social calendar.
